may Anantā, the destroyer of great obstacles, always protect [me]. || 84-45 ||
Whether in water or in a pit of fire, in fear of disease or fear of an enemy,
in fear of tigers or fear of thieves, or in the presence of great madness, fear, and the like— || 84.46 ||
In fear of the planets, in fear of the gods, and in fears arising from the Dānavas and mountains,
she is the fearless one, the one free from fear, the remover of fear, and the destroyer of fear.
May Mahābhīmā, Bhadrakālī, Bhairavī, Mārakāmalā, Mahābhūteśvarī, and Mātā, the sustainer of the world, protect us always. || 84-48 ||
May Mātṛkā protect [me] eternally in every land and at every sacred seat.
This armor-granting mantra bestows all perfections and destroys all suffering. || 84-49 ||
O Lord Mahākāla, O Hara! I have related this to you with great effort—that armor, difficult even for the gods to obtain, which one should recite upon rising in the morning. || 84-50 ||
He would be a conqueror of time, a god and not a mere human;
the glorious practitioner, whose essence is meditation, would himself become the Supreme Self. (84–51)
Having become firmly established in the lotus of command, one certainly becomes eternal;
it removes untimely death and enables crossing over the ocean of saṃsāra. || 84-52 ||

O Lord of the gods of gods, he who recites with supreme devotion this armor-mantra (kavaca), which is the essence of bliss and auspiciousness, shall certainly become liberated while living. || 84-53 ||
A fourfold garland of liberation remains firmly upon the neck of those foremost among yogis who have a guru that has reached the further shore of the Vedānta. (84–54)
He shall be a knower of the meaning of all scriptures, a lord who understands the meaning of the Yāmala;
having attained Śānti, Vidyā, Pratiṣṭhā, and Nivṛtti, he becomes stainless.
One whose self is united with yoga attains indeed the state of lordship; of this there is no doubt.
[This should be done] on a Tuesday or a Saturday, at a solar transit (saṃkrānti), or on a Sunday. || 84-56 ||
On the new moon day, during the *riktā* lunar phase, one should wear the auspicious armor;
a man on the right hand, and likewise a woman on the left arm.
One attains every accomplishment whatsoever that dwells in one's mind, having written [the mantra] with gorocanā, saffron, and lac. || 84-58 ||
One certainly attains accomplishment through the recitation of the yoga of Hākinī. || 84-59 ||

Thus ends the eighty-fourth chapter, titled "The Armor of Hākinī," in the dialogue between Bhairavī and Bhairava, within the section on Accomplished Mantras, in the *Mahātantroddīpana*, the latter part of the *Śrī Rudrayāmala*. 84.
Now begins the eighty-fifth chapter.
The venerable Ānandabhairavī said: "O fair-faced one, O lady of excellent gait, you who are the source of all knowledge!"
In the radiance of the heart of bliss, [there are] the limits of supreme bliss.
The meritorious armor has been told, which is a secret and exceedingly difficult to obtain;
it is not merely spoken of, but is to be realized through knowledge and practiced by means of the great net.
The armor of the Protector of Others bestows the accomplishment of omniscient gnosis;
now, O Ānandakulabhairavī, tell it to me with care.
Śrī Ānandabhairavī said:
"Listen, O Lord of Yoginīs, O Master of the Science of Yoga, O Lord!
[I shall speak] the ancient armor (kavaca) of the Supreme Lord, which is accessible through gnosis."
This essence of yoga is most secret and difficult to find in all tantras;
now, O Lord, I shall relate this supreme state with great effort.

Of this Great Armor (Mahākavaca) of the Illustrious Supreme Lord, Sadāśiva is the Seer (Ṛṣi), the Supreme Self (Paramātman) is the Deity, *hsauḥ* is the Seed-syllable (Bīja), Knowledge-Power (Jñānaśakti) is the Blissful Peg (Kīlaka), and the application (Viniyoga) is for the sake of attaining all desired goals. May the syllable *Oṃ*, the seed of the Vedas, always protect my head and wealth.
Hsauḥ! May the Great King of Pretas protect the skull at all times. || 85-6 ||
May the Lord of Hākinī, known as Sahāya, protect my hair and sense organs;
may the Supreme Deity of the space between the eyebrows protect the city of Vārāṇasī. (85.7)
May *ṣaṃ*, *raṃ*, *śaṃ*, and *vaṃ* protect me always; may *haṃ* and *kṣaṃ* protect the petals of the *bhūḥ* and *bhuvaḥ* worlds.
May the Bāṇaliṅga and the maiden of the brow-lotus protect me always. (85–8)
May Kālānala always protect that which is beyond the supreme and resides within the two petals;
may Tripurabhairava protect the cave of the eyebrows, which is eternal bliss. (85–9)
May Sarveśa, who bears the mark of the helpless, protect my three eyes;
may Abhaya Maṅgala protect the flickering tongue in the place called Dhruva.
May Pañcānana, who is as beautiful as the god of love, always protect my face;
and may Unmattabhairavendra always protect the pair of my cheeks. 85-11.
May he known as Hiraṇya, who dwells in the cremation ground, always protect the tips of my teeth;
may Mahādeva, the Great Space, always protect my ears. 85-12.
May Mañjughoṣa, known as Vikaṭa, always protect the region of the jaw;
may he who bears the blue throat and whose essence is the *praṇava* always protect my neck. (85.13)
May Aparājita, white in color, always protect the great impurity; may Tripurā, the Supreme Goddess, protect the region of the throat and the great space. 85-14.
May Mṛtyuñjaya, known as Ghora, and Viśuddha protect [me] always;
may Yogīśa, joined with the vowels and Īśvara, protect [me] always. (85–15)
May Vāmadeva, the Supreme Lord, always protect the heart;
may Īśvara, the Supreme God Sadāśiva, protect [me] at all times. (85-16)
May Aṭṭahāsa, together with ten million yoginīs, always protect [me];
may Akālacakra, the Omniscient One, and Avadhūteśvara protect my two arms. (85.17)
May Mahākāla, the Lord who is the husband of Bheruṇḍā, always protect [me];
may he who is the supreme beloved of Kākinī always protect the region of the flanks. || 85-18 ||
May Acyuteśa always protect my two sides;
may Atharveśa, the eternal bliss, the lord of the gods, protect my back.
May Tapinīpati, Īśāna, Vīrabhadra, and Yatīśvara—may Umāpati protect my navel region and my belly. (85.20)
May Gharghara constantly protect Rudra, the beloved of Rākiṇī;
may he who wears a mass of matted hair protect Rudrāṇī, the fierce deity. || 85-21 ||

May the Lord of Yogins protect my hips; may He who is the source of light protect the region of my waist; may He who illumines the interior of the six-petaled lotus always protect my *svādhiṣṭhāna*. || 85-22 ||
May Abhaya protect [me] always; may Bharga protect the four-petaled lotus;
may the Lord of Taruṇī always protect the location of Kuṇḍalinī and Ḍākinī. (85.23)
May the beloved of Pārvatī protect the anus at all times;
may Yajñanātha, the knower of his own mantra, always protect the pair of thighs.
May the Lord Dharmalakṣmīśvara always protect the pair of shanks;
may Mahākāla, the Lord of the Earth, protect the pair of soles of the feet. || 85-25 ||
May the boon-granting Vaṭuka, the illustrious Sadāśiva, protect my entire body;
may the Great Rudra, the Lord of Śrīpati, the eternally fierce one, protect me always.
In battle, in gambling, in dispute, in an empty house, in great fear, in the underworld, on a mountain, or in the forest—may the Lord of Vāgvādinī protect [me]. (85.27)
May Ghaṇṭeśvara protect me; may Murārīśa, who resounds with the conch, protect me;
may he who bestows supreme bliss protect me; and may he who seeks the welfare of others protect me on the path. 85-28.
May the Lord of Great Knowledge protect me; may the King of the Departed protect me—my son, my friend, my wife, my kinsman, and my own people as well. (85.29)
May Maheśvara, the support of all, in the form of the *liṅga*, protect [me] always;
may the Supreme Self protect the deity situated in the secret place. (85.30)
May Mahācandra, accompanied by his retinue, protect [us]; may he always grant protection.
May Mohana protect [us] in the rites of killing, expulsion, immobilization, and inciting enmity. || 85-31 ||
May the Supreme Lord, the Guru who dwells in the Pārijāta forest, protect [us]—he who is Sadāśiva in the acts of enchanting, liquefying, steadying, subjugating, and pacifying. 85.32
"May Sarvabhuk Kālarudra protect me everywhere. Thus has been declared this auspicious armor (*kavaca*), which bestows all spiritual accomplishments (*siddhi*). (85.33)
This armor, which bestows the accomplishment of the omniscient wisdom of the Lord, the Protector of Others, is difficult to find in the world and is concealed within all the tantras. (85.34)
O Lord of the gods, he who recites even once this *Yāmala*, which reveals day and night, becomes Rudra himself; of this there is no doubt. (85.35)
By the mere recollection of this, one certainly becomes increased in fame, glory, beauty, intelligence, and longevity; indeed, one becomes a king and a lord of yogis. (85.36)
He shall be a conqueror of desire and anger, a conqueror of death, and a great poet;
for him, there exists nothing whatsoever in the three worlds that is unattainable. (85.37)
Whoever should wear this auspicious armor on the throat or even on the head, having written it with red sandalwood or with saffron; || 85-38 ||
He shall become the son of a hero and the destroyer of tens of millions of great sins;
O Lord of Gods, he shall attain the perfection of yoga without effort. (85.39)
By reciting it one hundred and eight times, one obtains the fruit of the preliminary rite (puraścaryā).

Thus ends the eighty-fifth chapter, titled "The Recitation of the Armor of Paraśiva," in the *Ṣaṭcakraprakāśa*, within the *Siddhamantraprakaraṇa* of the *Mahātantroddīpana*, the *Uttaratantra* of the *Śrīrudrayāmala*, in the dialogue between Bhairavī and Bhairava. 85.
Now begins the eighty-sixth chapter.
Śrī Ānandabhairavī said:
[O you] who shine with the flow of the Vedic stream formed within the midst of the ocean of bliss!

O Beloved, who bestows perfect peace, whose splendor is the singular power that delights Yama and Dama; by Your divine grace of affectionate and blissful side-glances, quickly speak the wonderful and auspicious thousand-and-eight names of Hākinī from the Śrī Guru. (86-1)

The venerable Ānandabhairavī said: O Lord, O Guru, I shall tell you in person the entire auspicious and purifying Thousand Names of Śakti, which brings about well-being and consists of the eightfold knowledge and so forth.

O Lord, this which is to be served and studied by the lords of yogis desiring victory—being exceedingly secret due to their longing for the love of the Beloved’s arts—should be recited quickly in its entirety. 86-2.
Of this hymn consisting of one thousand and eight names of the goddess Śrī Parameśvarī Hākinī Mahāśakti, the venerable Paranātha, Sadāśiva is the seer (ṛṣi),
Gāyatrī is the meter (chandaḥ), the goddess Śrī Parameśvarī Hākinī Mahāśakti is the deity (devatā),
*klīṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), *svāhā* is the power (*śakti*), and the root-mantra of Siddhalakṣmī is the pinning-stake (*kīlaka*) located within the body.
The application is for the purpose of attaining the accomplishment of the knowledge of the Great Body (*mahākāya*).
Oṃ, Hākinī, Vasudhā, Lakṣmī, the supreme portion of the Self, the Transcendent, the Beloved of the Supreme, she who has transcended the Supreme, the Ultimate, the most beloved of the Ultimate. (86.3)
The Supreme Sovereign, whose love is supreme, whose nature is the Supreme Brahman;
the scorcher of enemies, the embodiment of supreme bliss, who serves the Supreme Lord. || 86-4 ||
Abiding in the supreme ether, she is the further shore who defines both the near and the far;
she is the supreme object of longing, the transcendent power, whose body is primordial, and who is radiant light.
The beloved of the lion-faced one, formerly the wife of another, now devoted to others;
having gone to a foreign land, she is the limit of supreme joy for her lord. (86.6)
Pārvatī is known by the name Parakulā, she who has eyes as beautiful as supreme collyrium;
she is Māyā, the beloved of the Supreme Brahman, and the illuminator of the Supreme Brahman. (86–7)
She is attainable through the knowledge of the Supreme Brahman; she is the beloved of the Lord of the Supreme Brahman;
she transcends the past and transcends the future, abiding in boundless majesty.
She is the one who rescues from the shoreless ocean; she is the one who delivers from the shoreless and difficult-to-cross [samsara];
she has the form of the flames of the supreme fire; she dwells between the eyebrows of the Supreme One.
She who is supreme among others, she who dwells in the field of others, she who is the supreme garland, the daughter of Parvateśvara, and she who is born from ten million supreme fires. || 86-10 ||
The shadow of others, the parasol of others, emerging from the faults of others,
the path of the supreme deity— such is love, possessing the luster of the crest-jewel of the five locks.
The fifth is the mistress of the lord of beasts, the fifteen-fold one, the beautiful fivefold one;
she who dwells in the Pārijāta grove and is fond of garlands of Pārijāta flowers. || 86-12 ||
She is distinguished by the division of the supreme and the non-supreme; she bestows the next world and liberation;
she has the form of the fire of supreme heat; she is the supreme woman and the reciter of the supreme mantra. 86-13.
The wielder of supreme weapons, the dweller in Pura, the Supreme Sovereign;
she who brings forth the radiance of love, and the bestower of devotion that is the lineage of love. || 86-14 ||
The city-dwellers are fond of the word "para" (other), she acts with supreme touch;
she is gracious, situated within the control of the Supreme, and she is gracious, wearing a garland of lotuses. 86-15.

She is fond of speaking kindly, she has attained the beyond, she is intent on the wealth of others' grain, she delights in the lands of others, she is drunk, and she is honored by those who are cowardly. (86-16)
She was one whose speech humbled others, who resided within the person, the Purañjanā;
she was mature, a remover of obstacles, an increaser of affection, and the beloved wife. (86.17)
She is the destroyer of the suffering of conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*) and has emerged from the essence of proliferation;
she has issued forth from the Purāṇas, she is full-bodied, and she is radiant with the beauty of her full breasts. (86-18)
Clad in silken garments, trailing silken threads, she delights in bestowing the wealth of others; she is devoted to the faith of others and intent upon the welfare of others. (86.19)
It is purifying, agitating the other, and destroying the essence of the other;
it reveals the very Supreme, illuminating the contemplation of the reality of the hidden meaning. (86.20)
Bestowing abundant wealth, she is seated upon two lotus petals;
her heart is full of joy, and she is established upon a gracious throne.
Richly adorned with a garland of radiant jewels, wearing a garland of radiant forest flowers,
possessing radiant compassion and bliss, she dwells within a radiant heart.
Delighting in supreme radiance, she is situated in the east, west, north, and south;
she abides in the wind, delights in drinking, and her body is supported by the wind.
She is dear to the Lord, she is the embodiment of the Lord, and she bestows devotion to the Lord;
she is the destroyer of supreme craving, she is the accumulation [of merit], and she grants birth after birth. (86.24)
She who has cast off another birth, she who effects the transition to another [state],
she who is born from another, she who is the celestial Pārijāta tree, she who is pure, and she who destroys the bonds of merit.
She is the remover of sin, the destroyer of tens of millions of evils, and the bestower of supreme liberation;
she delights in the atom, is subtle, and is the shatterer of atoms.
She who makes the subtle atom gross, who is higher than the highest,
who acts for the pleasure of Pūṣan, and who nourishes the three through Pūṣan.
Bhūpapālā holds a noose in her hand; she is Pracaṇḍā, the protector of life.
She consumes milk-stones and cakes, and is intent on drinking nectar. 86-28.
Her body is satiated with nectar, she is the act of churning the nectar, she has arisen from the ocean of nectar, and she yields milk as oily as nectar. (86.29)
She whose form is as pure as nectar, whose body is composed of nectar, and who delights in the restraint of the vital winds such as prāṇa, apāna, and samāna. (86.30)
She has the radiance of a portion of the wind; she bestows her own devotion arising from love;
she resides within a stone body, and her form is a mind of stone. (86.31)
She who delights in the western bliss, she who is the west, she who loves the west;
she whose body is as intense as the light-maker (the sun), she whose face is the light-maker, she who is radiance itself.
Suprabhā, dwelling in the wilderness, was fond of the means of endearment;
she remained there with her sandals worshipped by her former lord. (86.33)

She who has attained mastery over the sandals-mantra, she who recites the sandals-mantra, she who dwells in the auspiciousness of the sandals, and she who is the queen of the lotus-throne of the sandals. || 86.34 ||
Abiding at the edge of a mass of light red in radiance, possessing the brilliance of ten million fierce suns,
she is the supreme Hākinī who protects the three worlds.

Wisdom has faces both high and low; it bestows renown within the innermost reaches of the wilderness; it is intoxicated by the grove of the Pārijāta tree; and she is passionately fond of supreme intoxication. 86-36.
She is supreme joy and delight, flowing through the supreme ether;
she is the goddess of the supreme ether, the renowned Tripurasundarī. (86.37)

She who acts contrary [to worldly norms], who provides favorable assistance to the vital breaths (prāṇa), who is beloved by Prāṇarudreśvara, and who is the leader of the fierce attendants (gaṇas). || 86-38 ||
She is the nourisher, the protector of sons, grandsons, and others; she is the wearer of the *puṇḍraka* mark and possesses five chowries.
She is the consort of another, belonging to another, and the protectress of another’s lineage. (86.39)
Delighting in the supreme yoga, she deludes the bonds of the fettered beings with her noose;
she is the bestower of the fetters upon the fettered, worthy of worship, and the giver of the quality of grace. (86.40)
Residing in Prahlāda, her face like a full-blown lotus, she is supremely beautiful;
she is the supreme woman, the supreme garden, the full-moon night, and the beloved of the full moon.
Priyaṅkarī is the mother of the east; Pālanā is called the other;
Parāśarā is the abode of the good fortune of Parāśara; she is the beautiful-waisted beloved of the Supreme. 86-42.

She is accessible even in the cremation ground, she possesses a face as dear as the moon, she causes the falling of flesh, she is the Plakṣa tree, and she is worshipped by the hosts of monkeys. 86-43.

She who dwells in the Plakṣa tree, she who dwells in the sprout, she whose face is like a lotus, she who is clothed in raiment, she who stands in the form of a banner, she who is to be recited, and she who bestows purity upon the world. (86.44)
She is established in the recitation of purifying mantras, she dwells in holy places, her limbs are adorned with purifiers, and she wears a sacred body. || 86.45 ||
Tripurā is worshipped with supreme sovereignty, worshipped by all;
she is fond of meat and pleasing to the heart, and she delights in chewing straw.
She is protected by the hosts of the supreme goddesses, she is the mistress of the Rudra-tejas,
her face is like a full-blown lotus, and she wears a garland of blossoming lotuses.
She who loves flowers, whose lineage is of flowers, whose family is devoted to the noble flower;
she who dwells in flowers, who resembles a flower, and whose body is as delicate as a flower. || 86-48 ||
Pauṣpī, Pānaratā, Puṣpamadhupānaratā, Pracā, Pracayāhlādā, Prācanā, and Prāñcikā. (86.49)
She is the bliss of virtue beyond the womb, she who loves the quality of supreme generosity; she is the shoreless one, delighting in the sound of the infinite, and the awakener of the lotus-fiber.
She is devoted to awakening her beloved, she who deludes with a fierce roar;
she is full-bodied, the piercer of stout knots, and the remover of the dissolution.
She is the dissolution, the bliss of dissolution, and she who abides in dissolution;
she is the practitioner (prayoginī), skilled in application, the partisan, and the illuminator of the divisions of the sides.
She who possesses one wing and two wings, who grants the accomplishment of the five wings;
she who delights in the *palāśa* flower and wears a garland of *palāśa* blossoms.

She who performs the fire-oblation with *palāśa* flowers, who is seated upon a *palāśa* leaf, whose wings are vessels, who is clad in yellow garments, and who shines with a golden-yellow complexion. (86.54)
She who has swallowed the Kālakūṭa poison, she who has drunk the ocean of saṃsāra;
she who stands upon a lotus leaf like water, and she who dwells within a lotus petal.
She is a garland of lotuses, the remover of sin, wearing silken garments, supreme; she is the bestower of ultimate liberation, the highest hope, and the one whose command is unsurpassed. || 86-56 ||
She is the destroyer of the unpleasant, the protector of the conditioned formations of others,
the foundation, the honored, the accomplished, and the one who proclaims the well-known sovereignty.

She who grants success through effort, she who is agitated, she who destroys the qualities of phenomenal existence, she who is to be prostrated before, she whose disciples are living beings, and she who is dear to her established body. 86-58.
She is the one who destroys non-abiding, endowed with a pair of lotus feet, and she bestows life upon those worthy of worship through love and devotion for her lotus feet. (86.59)
The Paiśācī [speech] was cast aside by Pitṛśraddhā, the grandmother;
she was honored by Prapitāmahapūjyā, who was devoted to the svadhā offerings of the world of the ancestors.
She undergoes rebirth and lives again, remaining in the cycle of existence repeatedly;
she is very fond of eating the most excellent offerings and the like, and she is a witness to beloved things.
Known as the life-force of ten million suns, she abides in fire and is purifying;
she is the bestower of the goal of supreme knowledge and the accomplisher of the goals of those dependent on others. || 86-62 ||
She is the nature of the inward light, both the first and not the first dawn;
she is the morning twilight, the twilight of the earth, and the very embodiment of the supreme twilight.

The bestower of the supreme boon, the one who effects the determination of the knowledge of the vital breaths, the shatterer, the mistress of the pure radiance, she who brings about the intensity of spiritual practice. || 86-64 ||
She is the bestower of blossoming lotuses, the dawning before tranquility, the protector of the life-force of the mountains, and the witness to the foundation of the mountains. || 86-65 ||
She is the splendor that sustains the life of the mountains and acts as the parasol for the mountains;
she is the one who takes away [worldly] knowledge and is the witness to both dissolution and emergence. || 86-66 ||
Kālī is the mother of Prārabdha; Surā is the mother of Pradyumna;
she was formerly the wife of Sureśvara and the destroyer of the lineage of enemy heroes. (86.67)

She is the restrainer of enemy heroes and she who wears a garland of the *praṇava* (OM). She is the mistress of the *praṇava*, she who moves within the *praṇava*, and she who is fond of the first syllable of the *praṇava*.
She is pleased by the recitation of the syllables of the *praṇava*; she bestows the victory over death for those who possess vital breath;
she is adorned with the *praṇava*; she is wedded; and she is the gratification that devours the bound souls (*paśus*). (86–69)
She who removes the defects of cattle, who wields ten million Pāśupata weapons, who enters, who is named Praveśā, and whose three eyes are like lotus petals. (86–70)

She who finds bliss in the meat and liquor of animals, who is fond of sacrifices of ten million animals, who causes the destruction of the dharma of animals, who is noble, and who performs the satiation of animals. (86–71)
She inspires faith in the sacrificial victim (paśu), she is worthy of worship, and she wears a beautiful garland of animal heads;
she is trained in the yoga of the supreme hero and is a yoginī of the supreme philosophical system.
She has the axe, anger, and other primary weapons; she bestows the dissolution of the axe;
she wears a garland of rubies and is seated upon a ruby throne.
Adorned with ornaments of necklaces consisting of strings of rubies,
her lotus-like feet are graced by anklets and sandals possessing the supreme beauty of pollen.
She is the remover of all sufferings, adorned with golden necklaces, possessing deer-like eyes, abiding in Hari, the destroyer, possessed of beautiful necklaces, and the essence of existence.
Abounding in the splendor of necklaces and earrings, adorned with necklaces and armlets,
she is Hākinī, the one who seizes, and the illuminator of the rite of fire-offerings (homakarman).
Haridrā, Haripūjyā, Haramālā, Hareśvarī, Harātītā, Harasiddhā, Hrīṃkārī, and Haṃsamālinī. || 86-77 ||
She is the very nature of the Haṃsa-mantra, the piercer of the Haṃsa-maṇḍala;
she is "Haṃsaḥ So 'ham," she holds a jewel in her hand, and she is seated upon the king of swans.
Hīrakābhā, Hīrakasūkadhāriṇī, Haramekhalā, Harakuṇḍamekhalā, and Homadaṇḍasumekhalā. (86–79)
She is the delight of Śiva, the consort of the Lord of the Plow, she who arises from Hara;
she is the wife of Hara, devoted to Hara, resplendent with a form for universal destruction.

She is the abode of dissolution, the goddess Hālā, who is fond of the seed-syllable *hlīṃ* and the *praṇava*; she resides in the letters *ha*, *la*, and *kṣa*, stands upon the syllables *ha* and *kṣa*, is the goddess Hākinī, and the enchantress of Śiva. (86–87)
She who is the beloved of the singers Hāhā and Hūhū, who brings joy through her song; she who bestows the power of Śiva, who is fond of necklaces, and who wears a garland of diamonds. (86–82)
Resembling a diamond, abiding in a diamond, the support of Hara, situated in Hara, served by Hālā,
the destroyer of sin, she bestows the perfection of the Hintāla forest.
Mahāmāyā, Mahāraudrī, served by Mahādeva;
the Great Path, the Great Goddess, the Great Siddhā, and the Great Prosperity. || 86-84 ||
The great yoginī, the greatly auspicious one, the savior who is the sovereign of great yogins;
she who has the form of the great lamp-flame, the illuminator of the great lamp. || 86-85 ||
She is known as the Light of the Great Island, possessing great faith and great intelligence;
she is most exalted, the destroyer of delusion, the Great One, the Mighty One.
She is worshipped by Mahākāla, the sovereign lady of the Mahākāla family, the mother of the great lords of yogins, and the bestower of the accomplishment of delusion. || 86-87 ||
She delights in oblations and the act of offering; she is fond of the Hotṛ-veda;
she is a consumer of *haiyaṅgavīna* butter and is greatly beloved by those who enjoy *haiyaṅgavīna*.
She is in the form of an address: "O daughter of the Supreme Self!
O Goddess, beloved of Halanātha, the destroyer of the beneficial and the harmful! (86–89).
She is the destroyer of all sins, the bestower of the plow and its cause;
she abides in the guise of the plow and its cause, and she moves with the sound "hili hili."
She whose mouth is the sacrificial fire, she who is empty, the doe, the bestower of the system of Hari, she who delights in a forceful gait, she adorned with thorns, and the Earth (Ilā). 86–91.
Hillolā is the mother of Halāyudha and others;
she is Hemabahīṇī, Haimī, and Himasutā (the daughter of Himavat); she is as firmly established as the peak of the Hemaparvata mountain.
She is known as Haraṇā, the destroyer of attachment to Hari, the enchantress of Hara,
the mother of Hara, the wisdom of Hara, the utterer of the syllable "Huṃ," and the purifier of Hara.
The mother of Heramba, who dwells in the midst of the marketplace, white as snow, the kunda flower, and the moon, and who resides upon the Himalayan mountains. || 86-94 ||
Hotṛsthā, Hara-hālā, Helātītā, Ahargaṇā, Ahaṅkārā, Hetugartā, Hetusthā, and Hitakāriṇī. || 86–95 ||
She is the destroyer of misfortune, the slayer of the livelihood of those with false intellect,
fond of causes, the great night, known as day and night, and the source of Hara.

She who delights in worship and the like, she who is worthy of honor, she who causes the sound of "Alas! Alas! to resound, she whose form is established according to the *Hanumat-kalpa*, and she who bestows the spiritual accomplishments (*siddhi*) of Hanumān. || 86–97 ||
Halāhalapriyā, Aghorā, Mahābhīmā, Halāyudhā, she whose nature is the seed-syllable *hasauḥ*, and she who mutters the mantra known as *hasauṃ* called "Preta. (86–98)
Āhlādinī, Ihā, Ānandā, Arghyakrāntā, Harārcanā, Harabhītiharā, Ahaḥkā, Bījahaḥkā, and Hakṣarā. (86–99)

She is established in the yoga-perfection of Heramba, she is fond of sons such as Heramba, she is named Hanana, she is known by the name Hetu, and she bestows the application of perfection through forceful means (haṭha). 86–100.
Umā, Maheśvarī, the Primordial One, the bestower of infinite and boundless power, the support of all, the well-guarded one, the Sovereign, and Ugratāriṇī. (86–101)
Uṣeśvarī is supreme and the piercer of the upward-facing lotus;
she bestows prosperity and supernatural powers, and grants the perfect accomplishment of the seed-syllable of the subtle ether.

She who abides in curd, she who abides in ghee, she who possesses the sound of *tṛ*, she who resides in the seed-syllable *kharva*, she who is enriched by oblations of castor flower—she is intent upon the bestowing of sovereignty. (86–103)
She who loves the oḍrapuṣpa flower, whose syllable is Oṃ, who is fond of medicinal herbs;
she who is the essence of the sun, who is called Aṃśā, who resides in the letter Aḥ, and who is the tawny digit (kalā). || 86-104 ||
Residing on Kailāsa, she is the wish-fulfilling cow (Kāmadhenu); she is short-statured and holds a shield;
she is fond of wild flowers, she wields a sword, and she moves with the gait of a donkey. || 86-105 ||
The Gītagāyatrī is profound; the Gayā is weighty and most weighty;
it produces the sound of ten million clouds, rumbling and roaring with a terrible noise.
She possesses dense shade and a beautiful complexion; she is Caṇḍikā, the one with a lovely smile.
She has a face as beautiful as the moon and penetrates the meaning of the beautiful states of mind. || 86-107 ||
She possesses a parasol, she is free from deceit, she delights in the flesh of the goat;
she is the giver of victory, the living one, the kinswoman, and she is adorned by clouds.
The Victorious One, the Garland of Conquered Heads, the Resounding One, the One who Utters the *Jhañjana* Sound;
she who holds the *ṭaṅka* chisel, and she who bears the *ṭaṅka*, the arrow, and the bow. || 86–109 ||
Ṭhakurāṇī, Ṭhaṭhaṅkārī, Ḍāmareśī, and Ḍiṇḍimā; Ḍhakkānādapriyā, Ḍhakkā, Tavamālā, and Talātalā. (86–110)
Timirā, Tāriṇī, Tārā, Taruṇā, the bestower of the perfection of *tāla*, Tṛptā, Taijasī, and indeed Tulanātalavāsinī. || 86-111 ||

She who brings satisfaction, who possesses the scales, whose fragrance of oil perfumes the quarters of the sky, who is fond of what is substantial, who begins with the letter *tha*, whose form is stability, and who is perfectly firm. (86–112)
She who is the knower of the sound of the right body, the wife of Dakṣa, and born of Dakṣa;
she who destroys the fault of poverty and shatters formidable weapons. || 86-113 ||
She whose face is formidable with fangs, who possesses long and broad petals,
the mother of the gods, the army of the gods, she who is worshipped by the gods, and the state of compassion.
She bestows initiation and gifts, she destroys wretchedness, she possesses long, beautiful tresses;
she is the slayer of the lord of the Danujas and the one who humbles the enemies of the Danujas.
She is worshipped by the regions, the giver of inheritance, the bearer of the ten weapons;
she is the protection of servants, the protection of the land, and she who is both sky-clad and the direction itself.

She is pervaded by the rosy glow of the directions, she dwells in mountain caves, she is visible to those who seek her vision, she is the wife bestowed [by the Lord], and she is difficult to attain. 86-117.
Durgā, Dīrghamukhī, Duḥkhanāśinī, Divisaṃsthitā, Dhanyā, Dhanapradā, Dhārā, Dharaṇī, Dhāriṇī, and Dharā. || 86-118 ||
She whose face possesses enduring beauty; the giver of wealth; the mistress of grain;
attained through meditation; accessible through meditation; and the illuminator of the knowledge of meditation. || 86-119 ||
She is to be meditated upon, worshipped by the wise, Dhūmeśī, and the bearer of the burden;
she is the remover of the comet-like calamity, Dhūmā, who is to be meditated upon by all the lords of the gods.
She bestows the Dharma, its meaning, and liberation; she is the contemplation of the Dharma and the illuminator of the Dharma.
She is the form of dust and is white, and she bears a white parasol. || 86-121 ||
Clad in white garments and seated upon a white throne, she is white like the Himālaya mountain; she is the earth, the very act of spiritual accomplishment.
She is the daughter of Dhavaleśvara, with a face as radiant as a white path;
she is the daughter of Dhīra, the daughter of Dharma, and the bestower of certain success.
Her bliss is constant, her faith is constant, and her supreme contentment is constant;
she bathes in coconut water and sits upon coconut fruits. (86-124)

She is the woman, the consort of Nārāyaṇa, the sovereign; she is exceedingly fond of worship by those who bow before her; she is eternally devoted to men and gods, and is worshipped by the Gaṇas and Gandharvas. || 86-125 ||
She who dwells in hell and brings an end to hell;
the goddess who is a digit of the field of hell, residing in the nine sheaths. || 86-126 ||
She is the science of the stars, she is of the stars, and she abides within the circle of the constellations;
she brings about the rise and fall of kings, she is Nārāyaṇī, and she wears anklets.

She who brings about those fond of dance and song, she whose name is Navīnā (the New), she who lies within the Name, she who bears ever-new weapons, she who is eternal, and she who dwells in a forest of fresh flowers. 86-128.
Delighting in the love of fresh flowers, wearing garlands of fresh campaka blossoms,
adorned with necklaces of strings of fresh jewels, and possessing the luster of fresh gold.
She who is fond of salutations, she who destroys censure and the sound of musical instruments;
she who is a garland of wind-syllables, and she who is adorned with a wreath of wind-syllables.
She who causes fear through the defects of others, who abides in a manifest form, who wears a garland of blooming lotuses, and who dwells in love. 86-131.
She who is the seven horses of supreme bliss, she of broad hips,
she whose body is like a coral garland, she who possesses the limbs of desire, she who is the cloud, and she who has a hundred forms.

She whose form is compassion for those in distress, who inspires faith through the lineage of teachers, who is intent upon the performance of new undertakings, and who bestows the experience of the fruits of past actions. || 86-133 ||
She who brings about the perfection of love, a stream of love, beautiful as the waters of the Gaṅgā;
she whose supreme bliss consists of the merit of jackals, and who is satisfied by the feeding of jackals. || 86-134 ||

The goddess who bestows fruit and increases the fruit, who delights and gladdens with her fruit; she who wears a garland of serpents and is adorned with serpent-necklaces and other ornaments. (86-135)

She whose face is like that of a hooded serpent, who stands upon hoods, who is surrounded by a circle of serpents, who has attained a thousand hoods, and who wears a garland of full-blown lotuses. (86.136)
Vāsukī, worthy of worship by Vyāsa, fond of the worship of Vāsudeva, expressible as a portion of Vāsudeva, abiding in the speaker, and established in wealth (vasu). || 86–137 ||
She who holds the vajra-staff, the support, the one who subdues the viras, the accomplisher of debate;
she whose abode is the spring season, the stream of wealth, the bearer of the earth. || 86-138 ||
She whose guardians tremble, who protects her own form, who sits upon a bull, who is skilled in the love of Vivasvat, and who finds delight in the playing of musical instruments. || 86-139 ||
She is the illuminator of the science of ritual injunctions and the bestower of the established conclusions regarding those injunctions;
she knows the injunctions, is skilled in the Vedas, and elucidates the meaning of Vedic sentences.
She is worshipped by Baladeva, worshipped in her childhood state, the young girl Vasumatī, she who is to be known, the mother of the elders, and the beloved of the wise. (86.141)
The beloved of Bṛhaspati, honored by heroes, the moonlight for children, the protector of embodied knowledge, and the supreme one wearing a tiger skin. (86.142)
She is the destroyer of pain and ignorance, situated within the circle of emission;
she is worshipped with the ornaments of arrows, she wears a forest garland, and she dwells in the sky. 86-143.
The beloved of Vāmadeva, devoted to the worship and recitation of the left;
the auspicious one, bee-colored, the female bee, and possessing the luster of a bee. (86–144)
She who bears the crescent moon on her forehead, the formidable one, whose eyes are terrifying, who is both non-existence and existence;
she whose face is fearsome, whose body is fearsome, and who performs deeds of terrible prowess. (86.145)

She whose faith is formidable, she who is worshipped by the formidable, she who is exceedingly beautiful despite her fearsome form; she who grants victory in terrible battles, she who is the primordial Bhīmā, the Bhairavī of the formidable.
Bhairaveśī, Bhairavī, Sadānandādibhairavī, Sadānandabhairavī, and Bhairavendrapriyaṅkarī. || 86-147 ||

The wielder of the *bhallāstra* weapon, the daughter of Bhīma, the illuminator of the lineage of Bhṛgu; the consort of Bharga, the mother of Bharga, she who abides in destruction, and the devourer of destruction. || 86-148 ||
She who loves food, she who delights in food, Bhṛkuṇḍā, Bhāvabhairavī; she who bestows existence, she who grants existence, she whose power is existence, she who destroys existence. || 86-149 ||

Adorned with a tilaka of vermilion on her forehead, possessing beautiful earrings that illuminate her brow, and graced by the splendor of a garland of curls upon her forehead, she shines forth from the ocean of worldly existence.
She who removes the fear of worldly existence, who dwells within the orb of the crescent moon, who is beautiful with lotus-like eyes possessing black bees, she is Bhīmasundarī. 86-151.
She is fond of her devotees and beautiful in form, bestowing the accomplishment of the food of the inner state;
she delights in the moon of the eyebrows and pierces the lotus of the brows and the wheel of the *bindu*. (86.152)
She is the remover of the bonds of existence, the dweller in the terrifying forest of worldly phenomena;
she is the bestower of the perfection of mental yoga, the mental power that is greater than the mind itself.
She is the Great One, the devourer of fish, intent upon chewing fish;
she is devoted to the incarnation as a fish and intent upon chewing meat. || 86-154 ||
She who loves meat, she who is perfected through meat, she who delights in prepared meat;
she is Māyā, worshipped by the great heroes, and she who is clothed in space through her passion for honey-wine.
Mādhavī, whose waist is intoxicating, who partakes of honey and meat, who eats the fish-seal (mīnamudrā), and who heats the fish-seal. || 86-156 ||
Satisfied by the union of mudrās, she who has transcended the bliss of sexual union;
she who abides in liberation through the knowledge of sexual union, the great one who is not distressed even by a mighty buffalo. 86-157.
She is the faith in sacrifice, perfected through yoga, diligent, and the illuminator of effort;
she is Yaśodā, who delights in glory, established in youth, and the remover of restraint.
She who delights in the lover of the beautiful woman in the Rāsa dance;
she who bestows sovereignty; she who is beloved by the King of Night (the Moon); she who is as beautiful as Rāma. 86-159.
She is Rati and Aratirūpā, the Sarasvatī of the world of Rudra;
she is Rudrāṇī, Raṇacāmuṇḍā, and the illuminator of the Raghu dynasty. (86–160)
Lakṣmī, Līlāvatī, Lokā, born from ten million units of loveliness (lāvaṇya), Lokātītā, she who is called Lakṣaṇā, Liṅgadhārā, and Lavaṅgadā. (86–161)
Delighting in clove blossoms, dwelling upon clove trees, licking [the world], bringing about dissolution, she manifests a playful body. 86-162.
Lankā, whose lips are adorned with the beauty of lac, who bears a stream of jewels;
she who brings about the perfection of a hundred thousand recitations, and who reveals the mantra of a hundred thousand. || 86-163 ||
Vaśinī, Vaśakartrī, and Vaśyakarmanivāsinī;
Veśāveśyā, Veśaveśyā, Vaṃśinī, and Vaṃśavadhīnī. || 86-164 ||
She is the lineage-illusion, the deluder by the sound of the vajra, the embodiment of sound;
she is auspicious, composed of auspiciousness, the instruction, and the radiance of the moon-crested crest-jewel. (86–165)
She who grants fear by means of a pair of corpses, she who is terrifying with a pair of corpses;
she who dwells in a corpse, she who rests upon the chest of a corpse, she who illuminates verbal cognition. || 86-166 ||
She who pierces the six lotuses, the group of six, residing in the center of the hexagonal yantra;
she who bestows the essence of the six chakras, the essential one, [obtained] from the lake-lotus that is the essence of essences.
She is the destroyer of the *samanā* and other [winds], the bestower of accomplishment, and the remover of doubt;
she is worshipped in *saṃsāra*, the blessed one, and the witness of the seven mandalas. (86.168)
Sundarī, she who is fond of the beautiful, she who brings an end to the bliss of the beautiful;
she whose face is beautiful, she who possesses beautiful garments, she who bestows the perfection of beauty. (86-169)
Trisundarī, Sarvarī, and all [forms of] Tripurasundarī; Śyāmalā, Sarvamātā, and Svarā, who is fond of the state of friendship. (86–170)
Established in direct realization, she is the manifest witness, the witness of all;
she is Hākinī, the Mother of Śākinīs, the Śākinī who is beloved by Kākinī.
Hākinī is the mother of Lākinī; Hākinī is the beloved of Rākiṇī.
Hākinī is the mother of Ḍākinī; she is Harā, Kuṇḍalinī, and Hayā.

She who abides in horses, who dwells in the splendor of horses, who illuminates the seed-syllable *hasauṃ*, who resides in salt water, and who effects the breaking of the knots of the *lakṣa* [of the heart]. || 86-173 ||
She possesses the radiance of millions of suns; she is the creator of a hundred thousand universes;
she takes the form of moments, hours, and minutes; and she is the destroyer of the agitation of night.
She is beloved by the guardians of the fields (kṣetrapālas), the vaṭukas, Gaṇeśa, and the yoginīs;
she is the remover of the disease of consumption (kṣaya), the earth (kṣauṇī), and she is fond of the imperishable syllables situated in the cleansing place.
Established in the perfection of the vowels beginning with *kṣa*, she illuminates the consonants from *ka* to *ha*;
she is a mass of alkaline water and bitterness, the destroyer of the suffering of the earth. || 86-176 ||
The cessation of hunger, momentary knowledge, and the beloved who is transient—this, O Lord Kulaśekhara, has been declared regarding the Hākinī. (86-177)

The glorious one who, being self-restrained, recites this [text] consisting of the thousand names and its ancillary parts, accompanied by one hundred and eight [verses], is a yogi; of this there is no doubt. (86–178)
By the mere recollection of this, one becomes a hero and a lord of yoga;
yet, even in hundreds of millions of years, who could describe its fruit? (86–179)
Nor can it be told in full at once; listen briefly to its true fruit:
one attains long life and health, and gains confidence through the feet of the illustrious Guru. (86–180)
It brings about the attainment of the essence, is meritorious, purifying, and destructive of sin;
it burns away extreme suffering and bestows all forms of good fortune.
By constant recitation, the king of yogis attains the perfection of yoga;
the perfection of the body, the perfection of poetry, and the perfection of knowledge shall certainly come to pass. (86–182)
One shall attain mastery over speech, the power of the sword, and the state of moving through the air;
such a yogi becomes beloved by the three worlds and possesses the accomplishment of all desires and aims.
Having recited this great jewel which is not to be disclosed, one shall attain accomplishment;
even by its mere recitation, while fixing the mind upon the lotus of the eyebrows.
One attains fame and fortune, becomes a sovereign lord of kings, achieves the siddhi of the ḍākinīs, and brings the kuṇḍalinī under control. (86–185)
On an auspicious day, the supreme adept, whose nature is meditation, having become an ascetic,
should perform meditation upon the pericarp in the center of the lotus, which is the abode of the crest-lock (śikhā).
If one recites [the mantra] while meditating again and again upon the *cakrasāra* between the eyebrows, one attains the siddhi of Rākiṇī and obtains the vision of the deity. (86–187)
By reciting this constantly, one attains the accomplishment of fortune;
if one recites it while endowed with spiritual power (śakti), one attains direct realization.
The steadfast man brings Hiraṇyākṣī and Lākinī under his control if he rises at the end of the night and recites [this] in a temple of Śiva. (86–189)
If one recites this once at the conclusion of worship or at the conclusion of mantra-recitation, one attains the siddhi of a hero and brings the Kākinī under control. || 86-190 ||
One who is pure of heart and has conquered the senses should recite [this] throughout the night, whether on a bed, in the temple of Caṇḍikā, or in a house of honey. || 86-191 ||
On the fifth day, having risen at dawn with a purified soul, one attains the siddhi of the Śākinīs in every country and at all times.
On new moon days, especially on the day of Śravaṇā,
on the ninth day of the bright fortnight, and on the eighth day of the dark fortnight.
He who recites this while accompanied by his wife brings even a king under his control;
he who recites it alone in a secluded place becomes a conqueror of passion and possesses great strength.
And he who recites this during the remainder of the night shall become the best of practitioners;
he will be a donor equal to the wish-fulfilling tree and a conqueror of the gods—of this there is no doubt.
Having carefully established the yantra in the central space between Śiva and Śakti, the lord of practitioners, possessing stable resolve and omniscience, should recite [the mantra]. (86–196)

He who, dwelling in a place that is solitary, secluded, delightful, and conducive to the attainment of the fruits of ascetic success, recites this, shall obtain the fruit of liberation while living. (86–197)
Whether at an improper time or a proper time, one shall attain success after reciting it;
so too for one who recites it three times a day in a forest or at a crossroads.
The Lord of Yoginīs himself bestows the increase of longevity day by day upon whoever recites this even once—whether they be a fool or even a scholar. (86–199)
O Bhairava, one who is engaged in yoga shall quickly become a master of speech and will certainly be highly esteemed by reciting it just once. 86-200.
Having conquered Time, the Great Death, one shall attain devotion to the Goddess;
this is for those people who perform the pilgrimage after reciting [this] even once. (86-201)
Having attained the siddhi of beholding the Goddess, he shall obtain yoga;
whoever performs the sacrifice while reciting each name individually [shall achieve this]. (86–202)
He shall indeed become my son; he shall obtain the fruit of all desires, the fruit of all sacrifices, and, as a king among yogis, attain the perfection of knowledge.
If a person on earth—whether a lord of kings, a great adept, or a great poet—should wear [this] upon the neck, the head, or the right arm; 86-204.
By holding [the mantra] on the left arm of a woman, one shall attain all accomplishments (*siddhi*).
[This should be done] with *gorocanā*, saffron, and red sandalwood. (86.205)
O Maheśānī, one who is composed should write the mantra with barley-meal;
the Primordial Goddess certainly attains the supreme accomplishment of vital breath. (86-206)

Having recited [this] at the Liṅga on the Pūrṇimā day, on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, or on a Tuesday at midnight upon the Pīṭha, one becomes a possessor of the perfection of desire. (86–207)
What is not accomplished on this earth? By reciting this twelve times a year, one becomes truly ageless and immortal, and shall become the lord of ten million beautiful women. (86.208)
By reciting [this] for eight years, one attains the siddhi of entering the body;
by reciting it for merely six years, one becomes as wealthy as Kubera. (86.209)
By reciting it for even a single day every year, day after day, he will become a knower of the five principles and a knower of reality; of this there is no doubt.
O Lord, he who recites this seven times day after day for seven days shall dwell on earth for three kalpas, completely liberated from all evil.
By reciting this three times at night, the wise one becomes a sky-walker (*khecara*).
[This should be done] under Aśvinī during the bright fortnight and under Rohiṇī during the dark fortnight. (86–212)
If one recites it three times at night on the eighth or the ninth [lunar day],
or once during the day, he shall become a knower of the five principles (pañcatattvavid).
O Lord of Gods, without effort he attains the fivefold supernatural powers (siddhis) beginning with immortality;
it is certain that his union with the Khecarīs occurs eternally. (86–214)
In heaven, on earth, and in the netherworld, he certainly emerges in an instant;
he effects the paralyzing of fire, the paralyzing of water, and the paralyzing of wind. (86-215)
Whoever should recite this in a cremation ground according to the sequence of the five principles (pañcatattva),
he shall become a lord of the gods of gods, a scholar of the essence of the Siddhānta.
Combined with *śūkarāsava* or else with *kuladravya*,
one should worship according to the ritual procedure at the root of a *bilva* tree or at the base of the pedestal.
Thus the supreme Goddess, being gratified by the highest [means], becomes the bestower of spiritual accomplishments (*siddhi*).

Thus ends the eighty-sixth chapter, titled "The Arrangement of the Thousand Names of Hākinī," within the *Ṣaṭcakraprakāśa*, in the dialogue between Bhairava and Bhairavī, in the section on the Accomplished Mantras (*siddhamantra*) of the *Mahātantroddīpana* in the *Uttaratantra* of the venerable *Rudrayāmala*.
Now begins the eighty-seventh chapter.
The venerable Ānandabhairava said:
"O Ānandabhairavī, beloved of my life-breath, Sovereign of the Universe!
Through the words of your grace, the Thousand Names have been heard.
I now desire to hear the most wonderful and auspicious [teaching] concerning Hākinī, the Kula-yoginī, as intended by the Supreme Lord. (87-2)

This [practice] consists of the thousand names as an auxiliary limb, comprising one hundred and eight [verses], for the purpose of piercing the lotus of the eyebrows and for the attainment of the yoga of Hākinī. (87-3)

O Kulabhairavī, for the sake of attaining the supreme accomplishment through union with the Supreme Lord, speak to me out of compassion, being well-pleased, as this is the foundation for the attainment of dharma. (87.4)
For the protection of my body and for the sake of establishing my devotion to my husband,
O Yoginī, tell me quickly and in detail the means to remove great poisons.
"O beloved, tell me: by your grace, am I indeed the lord of the sky-faring Bhairavas and yogins in this region of the world, this fragment of the nectar-moon? (87.6)
Again and again I praise you; O Eternal One, may you alone be my beloved.
Śrī Ānandabhairavī said:
Now, O Lord of Yoga, O Lord of Life, O Sovereign of Yogins, O Bestower of Siddhis! (87–7)
Now I shall tell you for the sake of the perfect mastery over your own body; indeed, recite this always, and you shall bring death at any time under your control. (87-8)
Bound by the noose of affection for you, our Lord, out of compassion, she acted for the sake of obeying your command by destroying the Kālakūṭa poison. (87–89)
O Lord, listen to that thousand-name hymn titled *Nityāmṛtakhaṇḍarasollāsa*, for the sake of attaining enjoyment, liberation, ritual action, devotion, and spiritual perfection. (87–10)
For the benefit of yogins indeed, I shall now diligently proclaim the one hundred and eight names of the Siddhas, which is the means for determining the knowledge [of them].
Oṃ hsau sāṃ! He is the Supreme Lord and the Supreme Power, the Lord of the Beloved;
he is Śiva, the Ultimate, the Pāribhadra, the Sovereign of the Beyond, stainless and non-dual. || 87-12 ||
Self-luminous, without beginning or end, changeless, higher than the highest;
the Supreme Self, the supreme ether, the other, yet unconquered. (87-13)

The beloved of Pārvatī, the illustrious one, the kinsman of the distressed, the three-eyed, the soul of yoga, the bestower of yoga, the lord of the perfected ones, the hero, the ender of the vowels. || 87-14 ||

Kapileśa, the Guru, the one praised in song, the one who enchants with song, the beloved, the profound, the one established in the depths, and the one who brings delight through song and instrumental music. || 87-15 ||
The Guru-gītā-pavitra, devoid of honor through song;
the Lord of Gayā, the Lord of Datta, the auspicious Lord of Dattātreya. || 87-16 ||
He is the bearer of space, blue in color, possessing a body like blue collyrium;
he has the form of a bird, moves through the sky, is the very soul of the firmament, and dwells in the profound depths.
He is the giver of ten million cows, he who partakes of the milk of ten million cows;
he is the beloved of Abhayā, the glorious one, the Supreme Self, and the formless.
He who holds the number, who is formless, who delights in negation;
who subsists on air, whose form is air, who reaches the end of air, and who drinks his own air. (87.19)
The subduer of wind, the perfection of wind, the indigestion of wind, the knower of spring; the lord of dwellings, the protector of those in distress, and the sovereign sage among Nārada and others.
Nārāyaṇapriyānanda, Nārāyaṇanirākṛti, Nāvamāla, Nāvakartṛ, and Nāvasaṃjñānadhāraka. || 87-21 ||
Jalādhāra is to be known as Indra, the source of the qualities of the sense-faculties;
he is the form of fire, fierce and terrifying, the bearer of a garland of flames, and the Kula.

The moon is the glory of the lineage, the joy of the family, rich in splendor, and the bearer of the rays of the Vedas; it is the essence of light, the causal self, and the lord of the shadow of the cosmic age.
He is the knower of the supreme wisdom, the bestower of supreme bliss, the Lord conquered by Dharma;
he is the king of the lotus-like three eyes, possessing long eyes and captivating the mind.
Lord of Cāmuṇḍā, Lord of Pracaṇḍā, Hara who is the Lord of the Pāribhadra tree; the protector, the deluder, the guardian, the one abiding in secrecy, and the one worshipped by cowherds. || 87-25 ||
Gopanākhya, Godhaneśa, Cāruvaktra, Digambara, Pañcānana, Pañcamīśa, Viśāla, and Garuḍeśvara. || 87-26 ||
The Lord who is half-female, the Lord of mistresses, the ender of the Kula, whose form is destruction, and who is devoted to tens of millions of spirits and ghosts. || 87-27 ||
Ananteśa, Anantātman, Maṇicūḍa, Vibhāvasu, Kālānala, Kālarūpin, Vedadharmeśvara, and Kavi. || 87-28 ||
Bharga, Smarahara, Śambhu, Svayambhū, Pītakuṇḍala, Jāyāpati, Yājñavalkya, Vilāśīśa, and Śikhāpati. || 87-29 ||
Parvateśa, known as Pārvaṇa, the guardian of the field (kṣetrapāla), the lord of the earth, the venerable master of Vārāṇasī, the blessed one whose excellent vehicle is the bull. || 87-30 ||
Delighted by nectar, the charming one, the Lord of the forest-garland wearer, the beloved, the Lord of Kāśī, the Lord of life, the blue-throated Maheśvara. || 87-31 ||
He has a neck like a conch shell, he is the group of the ecliptic, the self of the groups, and the ruler of the waters;
his chest is like a water bubble, and he is broad, consisting of the lines of the ocean.
Lord of the earth, maker of the great, protector of the earth;
dwelling upon the earth yet worshiped by the earth, he was praised by the most excellent among mortals. (87.33)
Trident-handed, with a spear in his hand, the womb of the lotus, the bearer of gold;
the yogi established within the cavity of the earth, whose body is born of yoga. || 87-34 ||
He is the creator of the root of Pātāla, the protector of the lineage of Pātāla,
enriched by the garlands of nāgas of Pātāla, the giver of gifts, and free from agitation.
The slayer of the embryo, the Naga who committed sin, and the Naga Kāla;
the king who performed fierce austerities as Kapila, who was pleased [by them], and who acted for the benefit of the world. (87.36)
Worshipped by kings, established for the sake of kings, and the bestower of millions of royal benefits; satisfied by the worship of earthly rulers, he possesses great speed and is the Supreme Lord.
Beyond the far shore, even further beyond, he dwells in the great tree;
Rudra stands at the foot of the tree, the source of the fruit known by the name of Rudra.
The Lord of the power Raudrī, Krodhin, who has destroyed anger, Virocana, he who is endowed with the name "Innumerable," and who is devoid of transformation. || 87-39 ||
He is majestic, the support of the wind, praiseworthy, and the final arbiter of all things;
he is the reciter of the Vedas, the reciter of mantras, the deity, the guru, and the Lord.
Śrīnātha is the divine Guru, the Supreme Lord, the Guru, and the Master;
he is the Guru of the higher and lower, the possessor of knowledge, the knower of Tantra, and possesses the radiance of a hundred suns. (87.41)
He is fierce, the one who causes movement, existing in time, and stainless;
he is the fire of the Kālakūṭa poison, the stream, and devoted to the drinking of the mass [of the elements]. || 87.42 ||

He is enriched by a multitude of attendants, abides as the son of Parāśara, possesses the nature of the stabilizer (sthitisthāpaka), transcends all forms, and is the Lord of the stainless. || 87-43 ||
Patīśa, Bhāguri, Kāla, and likewise Hari;
Vaiṣṇava, Premasindhu, Tarala, and Vātavittahā. (87.44)
The Blessed One is the very nature of existence, devoid of space, eternal, imperishable, the Puruṣa, the witness, the infallible one who rests upon Mount Mandara. (87.45)
He who finds joy in the activities on Mount Mandara, who is born from the body of Vṛndāvana,
whose nature consists of both the expressible and the inexpressible, who is named Nirmala, and who is the destroyer of disputes.
The physician is one devoted to the Vedas, a text that illuminates the Vedic scriptures, rooted in the Smṛtis, possessing Vedic reasoning, and the manifest family deity. (87.47)
He is the examiner known as Vāraṇa, who dwells upon great mountains;
he is the bestower of love for Viriñca, the one who brings joy to his kin, and the beloved. || 87-48 ||
The bearer of Prayāga, the seeker of milk, the Gaṅgā of Gaṅgādhara, the Smara, the god beloved by the intellect of Gaṅgā, and he who is served by the bathing in the Gaṅgā. (87.49)
For he who stands within the waters of the Gaṅgā is a direct witness of the Gaṅgā;
he whose voice is like a jewel from the Gaṅgā wears a garland of jasmine flowers. (87.50)
Supreme with the fragrance of jasmine, bearer of the jasmine flower;
the great tree, the great hero, the great warrior, the great serpent. || 87-51 ||
He is great contentment, great nourishment, the bringer of auspiciousness to Mahālakṣmī;
he is the great ascetic, the great meditator, the great Caṇḍeśvara, and the Great One himself.
Mahādeva is the great joy, the illuminator of great intelligence, the great devotee, the greatly powerful, the great deceiver, and the one of great intellect. || 87-53 ||
He is the bearer of the great parasol, whose radiance reaches the pinnacle of the upholders of the Dharma;
he proclaims the bliss of non-duality, is liberated, fond of dissolution, and is neither liked nor disliked.
He possesses an exceeding fragrance and is beyond measure; he has reached the inner limit, O scorcher of foes;
he is one who has reached the end, who sustains the vital breath, and who discerns the subtle wind.
The god Hingulādeśvara is the great source of fear, the sphere adorned with great discernment, the bliss of nectar, established upon the sacred seat (pīṭha). || 87-56 ||
Nara is the lord of serpents, fierce, the master who grants the desires of his devotees;
he wears a garland of snakes, is righteous, performs daily rites, and acts for the benefit of his lineage. (87-57)
Śiśupāleśvara, Kīrtivikārin, Liṅgadhāraka, Tṛptānanda, Hṛṣīkeśeśvara, and Pāñcālavallabha. || 87-58 ||
Akrūreśa, the Lord, the increaser of affection, the increaser of the world, the most worshipful Vāmadeva, the formidable one, beautiful in passion. || 87-59 ||
Mahākāla, the one who delights his beloved, the playful one, the wearer of five crests, the lord of the primordial Śakti, the protector, the bearer of light, and the maker of radiance. || 87-60 ||
Moving with effortless grace, his intellect blossoming, he is honored by Nandin;
established in a stone form, his body is adorned with a garland of jewels.
The bestower of glory to the wise, the joy of the wise, the enlightened one who increases awakening;
the non-terrible, the destroyer of time, the stainless, and the one without support. || 87-62 ||
The lord of the power of the sacred seats (pīṭha), the bearer of love, the cause of delusion;
he is the peerless, the uneven state, non-existence, existence, and the one devoid of senses. || 87-63 ||
He who is without light, whose bliss is the cave, who dwells in the cave, and who is the lord of those who consume poison;
the lord of Durgā, the remover of difficulties, and he who is worshipped by the long-standing Siddhāntas. || 87-64 ||
Every lord of the fort was a Brahmin devoted to the worship of Brahmins;
he delighted in the joy of the twice-born and was absorbed in the meditative practice of Vedic rites.
He is the soul of the universe, the sustainer of the universe, and the fulfiller of universal consciousness;
he dwells within the inner faculties of the universe and is established as the very designation of the universe.

The support of all, the one worshipped by all, the one who dwells in all, the imperishable slayer of Indra; he whose food is the gourd, the protector of patience, the warder-off of obstructors. || 87-67 ||
Devoid of patience, he is the invocation that brings joy to Indra;
he is the person, the best of persons, residing in the potter's workshop, and the destroyer of the potter.
Abiding in the crooked, his life-force established in the sacred ordinances, he has reached the further shore of the bliss of sense objects;
he is the bestower of the knowledge of Brahman, a knower of Brahman, and one who has entered the inner qualities of Brahman.
Pālakeśa, Virāja, Vajradaṇḍa, the wielder of great weapons, the protector against all missiles, the bestower of prosperity, and the fulfiller of ritual and wisdom. || 87-70 ||
The noble son, honored by the king of the gods, honored by the sages, honored by the gandharvas, worthy of worship, and the destroyer of the knowledge of the dānavas. || 87-71 ||
Worshipped by the hosts of Apsarases and highly honored in the world of mortals;
the conqueror of death, the conqueror of enemies, the Plakṣa tree, the one who triumphs over death, and the lover of arrows.

He whose nature consists of the three seed-syllables, the blue-throated one, the lord of the earth, the destroyer of disease, the conqueror of enemies, the one to be served with love, the one accessible through devotion, and the effortless one. (87–73)
The effortless one, the delight of hell, the youth honored by enemies,
the unborn, the son of the gods, righteousness, the non-existent, and the slow-seated.
Gentle in his smile, gentle in his gaze, and delicately perfumed with a mild fragrance;
he has a necklace of rubies as his abode and is adorned with a string of pearls.
He is the giver of liberation and the giver of devotion, the bestower of the state of nirvāṇa;
he is free from conceptual construction, possessed of joy, devoid of fear, and the Great Person.
Abounding in garlands of pearls and coral, with a waist shining with a string of pearls; || 87-77 ||
Ratneśvara, Dhaneśa, the one dear as life to Dhaneśa, the one who lives by wealth, the one who lives by action, and he who is radiant with a body for destruction. (87–88)
Devoid of conventional knowledge of objects, he is a master of the great convention;
he is a supreme sage, a bestower of security, a giver of existence, and one who follows the lineage of existence. (87.79)
The lord of servants, the creator, the beloved of the Creator, the doer, the destroyer, the one who causes things to be done, and the refuge for both union and separation. || 87-80 ||
He is the disciplined master of yoga, the protector of faith, the benefactor of all beings;
he is the presiding lord of beings, the sovereign of beings, and is ever intent upon the protection of beings. || 87-81 ||
The bestower of prosperity and prosperity itself, the increaser of great prosperity;
the Lord of Mahālakṣmī, the beloved, the desirable, and the bearer of all arts. || 87–82 ||
The beloved of Kamalā, the Lord, Yama, the Immortal, swift as thought, the yogi of the mind, the yogi of honor, the breaker of pride, and the indefinable. || 87-83 ||
Delighting in the bliss of the unmanifest, he is defined by both the manifest and the unmanifest;
he is the Lord who finds delight in the Self, the protector of Kṛṣṇa, and the protector of Rāma.
The Lord of Characteristics, the Sustainer of the Hundred Thousand, the Lord of Bhāvatī, the Source of Creatures;
he who is named Bharata, the descendant of Bharata, Śatrughna, and the monkey Hanumān. (87–85)
The crest-jewel of monkeys, lord of the field-protectors, he who dwells within the quarters;
the lord of the directions, the sovereign of the lords of the quarters, the guardian of the quarters, indeed the sky-clad one. (87–86)
Adorned with an infinite crest-jewel, seated upon a throne of various gems, he is devoted to the bliss of pure consciousness; he is Vijaya, the son of Vijayā.
He is the deliberator upon victory and defeat, the Lord who is the crest-jewel of all states of being;
he wears a garland of severed heads, is the master of the lute, and the promulgator of the Sāra-tantra.

The protector of transmigratory existence, the living being, the possessor of the five vital breaths, the magnanimous one; he who is worshipful to him whose banner is Garuḍa, and he whose very form is the one whose banner is Garuḍa. || 87-89 ||
Gāruḍīśa, Mantriṇīśa, the benefactor of friendship and life; Siddhimitra, Mitradeva, Jagannātha, and Nareśvara. (87–90)
Abiding in the state of the Lord of Men (Narendra), he understands the practice of the state of Vidyā;
he is the Blessed One Kālāgnirudra, the sovereign Pracaṇḍeśvara.
The remover of misfortune, the enraged destroyer of enemies,
eternally blissful, the aged witness of dharma, and the bearer of the nectar-rayed moon.
Accompanied by his consort, he dwells among the ranks of his enemies; he is the slayer of the Daityas and the wearer of a shaven head.
Adorned with a garland of skulls and severed trunks, he is the illuminator of the Great Seed-mantra.
The invincible Lord of Yogas, beloved of Svāhā, the beloved of the Cause;
the giver of bliss to those dear to the Cause, the illuminator of the seed of the Cause. || 87-94 ||
Śrutikṣipra, Maṇirata, Brahmasūtraprabodhaka,
Brahmānanda, Jayānanda, and Vijayānanda.
Sudhānanda, Budhānanda, Vidyānanda, Balīpati,
Jñānānanda, Vibhānanda, Bhāvānanda, and Nṛpāsana.
He is the bliss of all postures, the bestower of joy to the world,
the bliss of fullness, the bliss of existence, and indeed the bliss of nectar.
Śītala, who remained for eighty years, was the one who established the formal rules;
he was Śīlāḍhya, Suśīla, Śīlānanda, and Parāśraya. (87–98)
Easily obtained, he is the delight of sweetness, intoxicating with the fragrance of sweetness;
indivisible, moving within the urine, known as Strife, he is formidable.
Rich in the sound of bellowing, supreme bliss, intense and uneven bliss,
the sovereign intoxicated by wine, he who commands the Gandharvas while they are in a state of intoxication.
The giver of glory with a hundred crores of arrows, possessing a splendor equal to ten million heroes; the unborn lord of the night, worshipped by the uneven-rayed sun. || 87-101 ||
Lord of knowledge, Lord of the Vedas, of immeasurable prowess;
Lord of the Rākṣasas, Lord of great heroes, who bestows love and assistance.
Vāraṇāvipriyānanda, Vāraṇeśa, Vibhusthita, Raṇacaṇḍa, Raśeśa, and the Lord Raṇarāmapriya. || 87–103 ||
The lord of battle, the delight of combat, whose body is the corpse of war;
the devotee of the Goddess, the god of gods, who is intent on fierce deeds in heaven.
Khaḍgī, Kavacī, Siddha, Śūlī, Dhūli, Triśūladhṛk, Dhanuṣmān, Dharmacitteśa, Acinna, Nāga, and Sumālyadhṛk. (87–105)

He is the meaningful, the one who loves the meaningless, the rarely attained, and he who has transcended impurity; he is exceedingly beautiful, enriched with gold, wearing a golden garland, and possessing a command marked by golden peaks.
The conqueror of Kandarpa, the Lord of Kapittha, he whose crest is the sun;
he who possesses the fragrance of a lotus, the one of most excellent scent, the bearer of the moon-crested Lord, the blissful one. (87–107)
He whose abode is the support of the purifier, who bears the excellent seed-syllable like a scholar,
whose form resembles Kandarpa, who is the conqueror of Māyā, and who wears a tiger skin.

Richly adorned with the crest-jewel of supreme beauty, fond of the variegated jewels of serpents, possessing magnificent temples, Kumbhakarṇa, the conqueror of Kurujetā, and the lord of poets. (87–109)
He has one face and two mouths; he is twofold as the teacher of the Vedas;
he is self-supported and composed of the Guru; he is the bestower of the Guru-mantra. || 87-110 ||
The Lord of Śauri, who follows the path of knowledge, who follows the path of the perfected ones, who moves with fierce speed;
he who dwells in names, who dwells in sacred fields, who is the field itself, and who pierces the knots of the sky. (87–111)
Clad in the hide of an elephant, he is the protector from the hide of an elephant;
he is profound and exceedingly subtle, fond of song and instrumental music, and sweet-spoken.
He causes an abundance of joy, is ever-delighting, and moves according to the mind; he is dear to Śiva and Śakti, dark-complexioned, and the supreme kinsman.
He who always acts for the pleasure of guests, the Lord of Govinda, the Sovereign of Hari; the Lord of all, the Protector of women yet to be born, the Womb of Knowledge, and Vibhāṇḍaka. || 87-114 ||
He is the creator of the form of the cosmic egg and the upholder of the dharma of the cosmic egg;
he is the ocean of dharma, the path of dharma, and the bestower of the perfect accomplishment of the contemplation of dharma.
He is established in non-abiding yet is a believer; he is well-being itself and speaks according to his own will.
He is the form of food, he dwells within food, he is the giver of honor, and he is of great mind.

The Lord of primordial power, the one who sets in motion the network of the letters of the Mother (Mātṛkā), he who is worshipped by the Mātṛkā-mantra, and the bestower of perfection through the Mātṛkā-mantra. || 87–117 ||
Beloved of his mother, honored by his mother, the sovereign of the mandala of mothers;
the destroyer of delusion, the bestower of delusion, abiding in delusion, and the lover of delusion. || 87-118 ||
Thus has been told, O Lord, this auspicious thousand names, consisting of one hundred and eight, which is of great merit, leading to heaven, and difficult to obtain on earth. (87–119)
By the mere hearing of which a man becomes Nārāyaṇa;
it is a great secret not to be revealed, beyond even the range of the gods. (87–120)

The fruit of one who, having performed the recollection of this form, becomes a yogi who has reached the further shore of yoga, cannot be described by the wise even in hundreds of millions of years. (87–121)
He is the master of all accomplishments in the three worlds, including the mobile and the immobile;
and there are many gods and yogins who contemplate the ultimate reality.
By reciting and retaining [this], the knower becomes a destroyer of great sins;
he certainly becomes augmented with long life, health, and prosperity. (87–123)
Whoever recites this even once during battle, in fear of malevolent planets, in a great forest, or in the danger of water, shall become beloved by the gods.
Having performed worship with special care, he who recites this regularly and with purity becomes, in an instant, the king of yogins who shatters the minds of all. (87–125)
He shall become the protector of all the worlds and attain supreme bliss—he who recites [the mantra] at a single seat, especially at Kāmarūpa. (87–126)
By reciting it three times a day or even six times a day, one becomes a king among yogins;
one attains the siddhi of traveling through the sky as well as the siddhi of the medicinal pill.
The supreme practitioner indeed attains sovereignty day by day;
he who recites this constantly at all times becomes omniscient and possesses an intellect as sharp as the tip of a blade of kusha grass.

The best among yogis on earth, the conqueror of desire, shall certainly—whether ignorant or possessed of knowledge, or whether without wealth or possessing wealth—become [perfected] instantly. (87-129)
He who wears this with devotion around his neck or on his right arm shall always receive honor from kings; indeed, for him there is no death. (87–130)
Success shall be attained by him before long; there is no need for deliberation on this point.
Having become the Lord Avadhūteśvara, he shines forth—of this there is no doubt. (87–131)
With unadulterated red sandalwood, along with turmeric and saffron,
and with stalks of *sephālikā* flowers together with masses of petals, || 87-132 ||
Whoever, having gathered [the ingredients], should write this hymn using only sandalwood water, shall become a son of Pārvatī either in an instant or within twelve days. (87–133)
Having maintained the recitation of the Thousand Names for one month, two months, three months, or even a year, he becomes liberated while living. (87–134)
Having recited it twice that many times, one obtains merit a hundred millionfold;
what more need I say? One shall become a sovereign lord of the entire world.

He who recites this essence of the hymn here becomes a lord of the hosts in the three worlds, a master of yoginīs, and rich in wealth; with a mind of perfectly pure disposition, he shall dwell for a long time as the beloved of Bhavānī.
The subject matter consists of one thousand and eight [verses] of knowledge.
Thus, in the *Śrī Rudrayāmala*, in the *Uttaratantra*, in the *Mahātantroddīpana*, in the section on *Siddhamantra*, in the *Ṣaṭkoṇaprakāśa*,

in the arrangement for piercing the *bhrūpadma* (the lotus between the eyebrows), in the dialogue between Bhairavī and Bhairava, in the recitation of the *Paraśiva-hākinīśvara-aṣṭottarasahasranāma* (the Thousand-and-Eight Names of Paraśiva-Hākinī).
The eighty-seventh chapter. || 87 ||
Now begins the eighty-eighth chapter.
The venerable Ānandabhairavī said:
"Listen, O Supreme Lord, to that which is difficult to obtain within the circle of yogis."
The essence of the knowledge of Mahāyoga, the auspicious blessing of the three worlds. || 88-1 ||
By the mere knowledge of which, whether he be a practitioner or even a non-practitioner, the wise one becomes a conqueror of death and partakes in the nature of supreme bliss. (88-2)
The place of the fire-oblation (homa) is in the middle of the crest-lock (śikhā), and that of the lamp is between the eyebrows;
she who is the nature of the Supreme Brahman, whose form is the crest-lock, is beloved by the world. (88-3)
O Lord, the wise one, having mentally contemplated the power of Svāhā there, should complete the accomplishment of the fire-offering ritual every day after offering praise. || 88-4 ||
This is the supreme knowledge; hear now another knowledge, O Lord:
above the crest [of the flame] is the Supreme Śakti, whose nature is the Supreme Brahman.
Camel-faced and red-faced, resembling the fire of ten million kalpas;
having meditated upon her in the pericarp of the lotus of the family, the one of great mind— || 88-6 ||
The Goddess, who bestows supreme bliss, abides in union with the mind;
she dwells in a state subtler than the subtlest, yet possesses a form more massive than the most massive.
She who has transcended time, whose form is time, who illuminates both time and non-time;
she is the source of Dharma, radiant, and the sovereign of skill in composition.
Pārvatī, the elephant of battle, whose gait is like that of an elephant,
the supreme one who bestows the perfection of liberation, the sustainer, and the illuminator of the five principles.
The fifth [syllable], situated in the fifth [position], is fond of speaking the five faces;
it possesses five rays and is beautified by the garment of the directions.
She wears garlands of moonstones and sapphires with tips as thick as young sprouts;
she has two arms, is observant of silence, and holds a book of knowledge.
Having meditated upon the supreme goddess Raudrī, who abides in a single form,
one should [visualize] the mandala of the hundred yoginīs constantly in its four directions.
The mandala, beautiful with the shape of a row of wheels, is situated within the pavilion;
I shall state their names—listen, O beloved of Bhairava! (88–13)
Durgā who dwells in the cremation ground, the deer-eyed Pracaṇḍikā, Raudrī, Śyāmā, Yoginī, Śivānī, and Śivamohinī. || 88-14 ||
Sukhinī, Pañcamī, Bālā, Kuṭilākṣī, Vasundharā, Suvarṇāṅgī, Pāvanā, Pavitrā, and Paramānanā. || 88-15 ||
Siddhidā, Maṅgalā, Bhāvyā, Surati, Kāmadā, Rati, Prabalā, Vimalā, Camanā, Prabhā, and Kāñcanamālinī. (88–16)
With her body bent in three places, her limbs dark-complexioned, youthful, and tremulous;
she is easily attained and yet difficult to attain, and she is like a fully blossomed lotus. (88-17)
Pātālamukhī, Gomuṇḍā, Ghorahāsā, Vilāsinī, Aruṇā, Śravaṇā, Mantrī, Mālatī, and likewise Mallikā. (88–18)
Vaiśvānarī, Bharadvājā, Trivibhāgā, Mati, Kṣudhā, Subhadrā, Bhākarī, Liptā, Nartakā, and Ciṭisundarī. (88–19)
Bṛhannalī, Bhāgavatī, Viśālā, Virālā, as well as Mānasī, Vānarīgrīvā, Krodhinī, and Mohinī. (88-20)
